author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page below the first as the first page
summary: A request naming a page below the first shows the first page of owner matches and the normal listing, rather than an error page.
acceptance_criteria: given a request naming page zero, when the owner listing runs, then the first page of matches is listed rather than an error page
given a request naming a negative page, when the owner listing runs, then the first page of matches is listed rather than an error page
given a request naming no page at all, when the owner listing runs, then the first page of matches is listed as before
non_goals: page values beyond the last page
page values that are not whole numbers
paging behavior on the veterinarian directory
notes: Owner intake recorded no decisions beyond the request; the request is quoted in the intake-decision at line 1. Today's error page for a page below the first also breaches REQ-SYS-002. Open question recorded in docs/prd.md for pages beyond the last and for non-whole page values. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Cause: OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName builds PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) from the raw request parameter. For page <= 1 the index is negative and PageRequest.of rejects it, so the IllegalArgumentException escapes the handler and the error page renders. Durable memory already places the fix: security-principles.md section Trust Boundaries requires range validation of external input at the boundary, and the Web controller row of architecture-principles.md assigns request binding to the controller. Normalizing a page parameter is boundary input handling, not a business rule, so it does not extend the controller-rule deviation that system-design.md section Package Structure records. The same method already normalizes a missing lastName to the empty string; the page clamp is that shape applied to a second parameter. No new pattern, package, or type; docs/system-design.md and the ADRs need no edit.
integration_points: addPaginationModel publishes currentPage, which src/main/resources/templates/owners/ownersList.html uses for the numeric page list and the first/previous/next/last links; the clamped value must be the one published

patterns.description: existing request-parameter normalization in processFindForm: a missing lastName becomes the empty string before the query runs; clamp the page at the same site, once, so the query and the model agree
WebMvcTest plus MockitoBean OwnerRepository listing test shape; stub findByLastNameStartingWith with a two-element PageImpl so the single-match redirect does not fire

risks.risk: Clamping inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName alone fixes the exception but leaves currentPage at the raw value, so the pagination widget disagrees with the content shown
risks.mitigation: Clamp once at the top of processFindForm, before both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel

risks.risk: The repository is stubbed with any(Pageable.class), so a test asserting only HTTP 200 passes even when currentPage stays 0
risks.mitigation: Assert model attribute currentPage equals 1, and capture the Pageable to assert a zero page index

risks.risk: VetController.findPaginated carries the identical page - 1 arithmetic, so /vets.html?page=0 fails the same way
risks.mitigation: Out of scope: the prd-entry lists veterinarian paging as a non-goal. Leave it untouched and raise it as a separate slice

notes: Basis for the covering-code claim is grep over the owner package and the Thymeleaf templates; no IDE oracle was connected for this dispatch, so this is the weaker basis. Acceptance criterion three (no page named) already holds through the defaultValue of 1 on the request parameter; its test is a regression guard, not a change. A non-numeric page value still reaches the error page through binding type mismatch, which the prd-entry lists as a non-goal and docs/prd.md carries as an open question. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit found nothing.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Class sweep for the pattern this slice fixes: `showVetList` takes the same unclamped `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page` and passes `page - 1` straight to `PageRequest.of`, so GET /vets.html?page=0 (or a negative page) still throws IllegalArgumentException and renders templates/error.html for any unauthenticated visitor. After this change the codebase secures one boundary-input concern two different ways (owner listing clamps, vet listing does not), which is the Pattern Consistency divergence the security checklist flags. Harm is bounded and low: error.html renders ${message} but Spring Boot's default server.error.include-message=never leaves it blank, so the exposure is an attacker-triggerable 500 rather than a stack trace or internal detail leak. Not a defect in this diff - the vet listing is outside the change set and outside REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001's stated scope - so it is a scope question, not a fix request.

recommendations: Supply chain was NOT verified against the NVD in this review: the project configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin (build.gradle declares java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm native 1.1.2, cyclonedx-bom 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47) and this reviewer has no network access. The diff changes no dependency and no build file, so nothing new entered the supply chain, but a human or CI should close the CVE check against Spring Boot 4.1.0's managed set. The cyclonedx SBOM task already produces the artifact an external scanner would consume.

Consider recording the vet-listing parity question (clarify finding above) alongside the existing PRD Open Question about pages beyond the last page and non-whole-number page values, so all three unhandled page-parameter shapes are tracked in one place.
approved_aspects: The change strictly reduces attack surface: a request-controlled int that previously reached PageRequest.of as a negative index (unhandled IllegalArgumentException -> error page) is now clamped at the boundary, converting an attacker-triggerable 500 into normal listing output
Clamp is applied once at the method entry and both consumers (findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel) read the clamped value, so no path can reconstruct the unvalidated input

Math.max(page, 1) cannot overflow, and the upper end is safe: PageRequest.getOffset widens to long before multiplying by page size, and an out-of-range high page yields an empty Page handled by the existing notFound branch, so there is no unbounded allocation or integer-overflow path

No new trust-boundary crossing: no file I/O, no shell or process execution, no SQL/LDAP string interpolation, no serialization or Jackson configuration, no reflection, no regex, no logging of request-derived values
Model attribute currentPage is an int rendered through Thymeleaf's default-escaping th:text, so no user-derived content reaches HTML unescaped
No secrets, tokens, credentials, URLs, or configuration values introduced in the diff; no /tmp usage
OwnerController remains a stateless singleton - the new member is a private static final int constant and requestedPage is a method local, so no shared mutable state was added
Test-only additions (ArgumentCaptor, @ParameterizedTest) carry no production or runtime security impact

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owner-listing page parameter to the first page

blast_radius.note: One module and three files: a two-line clamp inside OwnerController.processFindForm plus its tests and the PRD entry, no sensitive paths, no config, dependency, schema, or template change, and no caller outside the one handler method.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do exactly what the summary says: requestedPage = Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) computed once at method entry, and both downstream consumers (findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel) read the clamped value, so no path reconstructs the raw parameter and the widget cannot disagree with the content; behavior for page >= 1 and for the absent parameter is bit-identical to before.

test_adequacy.note: The tests would fail against a plausibly-broken implementation: each asserts both model currentPage == 1 and, via an ArgumentCaptor on Pageable, a queried page index of zero, so clamping in only one of the two places is caught; all three acceptance criteria (page=0, page=-1, no page) are driven through real MVC dispatch with MockMvc.

reviewer_hedging.note: Three roster reviewers approved with empty findings, but the security-reviewer (dispatched beyond the planned roster) approved with a clarify finding and two recommendations: VetController.showVetList keeps the identical unclamped page - 1 arithmetic, so /vets.html?page=0 still throws and renders the error page after this merge, and the supply-chain CVE check against Spring Boot 4.1.0 was not run for lack of network access.

scope_deviation.note: The diff lands exactly on the two file targets the prd-entry declared plus the PRD itself, with zero build retries, zero consultations, and zero design revisions; the vet-listing parity gap was explicitly left untouched as a declared non-goal rather than drifted into.

rationale: The clamp itself is textbook-safe and the tests pin both the queried index and the published page, so merge with confidence. What deserves the read is the residual the security reviewer parked: the identical page - 1 bug survives in VetController, leaving one input concern handled two ways. Decide whether that follow-up slice is filed before merging.
